iOS 27 is a major update to the Apple Photos app, with improvements to slideshows, shared albums, and more, while also adding a long-awaited camera roll-like feature: "Captured by Me."

The "Captured by Me" section in the iOS 27 Photos app will only include photos and videos you take with the Camera app

Apple's Photos app has steadily expanded its features over the years. In addition to storing photos taken with your iPhone, it also displays content shared with you by friends, Memories, screenshots, saved media, and more.

Previous versions of the Photos app once had a "Camera Roll" feature similar to today's "Recents" album, which would display photos you had taken as well as images you had saved.

But there has always been a lack of a feature that truly only shows photos and videos you took yourself—in other words, something more appropriately called a "Camera Roll."

iOS 27 brings this long-missing feature, called "Captured by Me."

The "Captured by Me" section in iOS 27 is a brand-new album category that, as the name suggests, only includes media you captured with the Camera app.

That means photos and videos you take with your iPhone will all be gathered in one place, but you won't see screenshots, images sent by friends, or other types of content.

In addition to having this dedicated "Captured by Me" category, you can also use the "Captured by Me" filter in the main photo library.

No matter how you use this feature, "Captured by Me" in iOS 27 fills an important gap in Apple's photo album functionality.

Are you looking forward to using this brand-new Apple Photos feature in iOS 27? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
